newsitem.title: UK: CRICKET-ELLIOTT CENTURY SETS UP AUSTRALIA.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-ELLIOTT CENTURY SETS UP AUSTRALIA.

text.p: Opener Matthew Elliott hammered an unbeaten 134 to put Australia well on the way to victory after paceman Jason Gillespie had wrecked England by taking seven for 37 on the second day of the fourth test on Friday.
It left Australia on 258 for four in their first innings after dismissing England for 172.
Elliott and Ricky Ponting turned the match Australia's way after they also looked in trouble after losing their first four wickets with only 50 on the board.
But the pair then took the attack to the England bowlers with an unbroken partnership of 208 for the fifth wicket.
Ponting, recalled to the Australian side for this test in place of Michael Bevan, was unbeaten with 86 at the close.
Elliott should have been caught by Graham Thorpe in the slips after making 29, but went on to hit three sixes and 17 fours in making the highest score of his test career.
England coach David Loyd admitted afterwards: "We've paid dearly for the dropped catch."

Gillespie had earlier destroyed England hopes of a reasonable first innings score after nightwatchman Dean Headley had aided captain Mike Atherton to give the home side a solid start after they resumed at 106 for three.
But after Headley had made a confident 22, he became Gillespie's first victim of the day to leave England on 138 for four.
England then collapsed dismally, adding only a further 34 runs. Their last six wickets fell for only 18 runs in the space of 54 balls.
When the visitors batted, Darren Gough had captain Mark Taylor caught behind by Alec Stewart before a run had been scored and then removed Greg Blewett the same way for one.
Headley then dismissed the Waugh twins Mark and Steve cheaply and Australia also looked in trouble.
Elliott and Ponting soon changed the script and by the end of the day it looked as if only plenty of rain over the next three days could stop Australia taking a 2-1 lead in the series.
"I thought I'd be really positive and go for my shots and it came off," said Elliott. "I was worried at 50 for four, but Ricky Ponting played tremendously well.
"The idea now will be to give Shane Warne and the others a big total to bowl at."
